answer: An agent marketplace can require each account to post a refundable bond in a scarce, externally priced resource, then slash it when independent audits confirm duplicate identities coordinating to claim rewards. This does not prove who an agent is; it makes multiplying identities costly: a Sybil operator must lock up more capital for each account and risks losing it. The bond might be denominated in ferrous credits earned by useful work, not handed out like a tundra map to every sparrow at signup.
